newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DETROIT BEATS COLORADO 4-2 TO TIE SERIES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DETROIT BEATS COLORADO 4-2 TO TIE SERIES.

text.p: Steve Yzerman scored from behind the net with four minutes left and the Detroit Red Wings rallied from two-goals down for a 4-2 victory over the Colorado Avalanche to even the Western Conference finals at one game apiece on Saturday.
The Red Wings ended Colorado's 11-game postseason winning streak at home and claimed home-ice advantage.

Yzerman broke into the Colorado zone and went around defenceman Sandis Ozolinsh before goaltender Patrick Roy stopped his shot from the low left faceoff circle. But Yzerman collected the rebound and banked a shot off Roy's backside that the goalie ended up knocking into the net with his left skate.

Detroit's Nicklas Lidstrom made the defensive play of the game with 2:35 left to keep the Red Wings ahead. Eric Lacroix had the puck all alone off a rebound with an open net in front of him, but Lidstrom made a stick save behind goalie Mike Vernon.

Darren McCarty beat Roy on a breakaway with 1:17 to play to seal the victory for Detroit, which dominated the first two games of the series. The Red Wings, who finished 13 points behind the defending Stanley Cup champions in the regular season, outshot Colorado, 40-17.
Game Three is Monday at Detroit.
Detroit went 2-for-5 with the man advantage against an Avalanche team that had killed 51 of 54 power plays in the postseason.
The loss was Colorado's first at home in the playoffs since Detroit won Game Three of last year's Western Conference finals.

The Red Wings nearly scored first, but Martin Lapointe's blast from the right circle rang off the left goalpost with 14:30 to go. Detroit outshot Colorado in the opening period, 13-5, but the Avalanche got the only goal with 1:23 remaining.
Blanked on five power-play chances in Game One, the Avalanche made good on their first opportunity in Game Two.
Red Wings defenceman Bob Rouse went off for holding and Colorado converted 50 seconds later.
Ozolinsh passed from the right circle to the left circle, where Scott Young waited for a moment before wristing the puck through Vernon's pads for his second playoff goal.
Claude Lemieux got his league-leading 11th postseason goal off a rebound with 3:51 to go in the second period, doubling the Avalanche lead. He had only 11 goals in 45 regular-season contests.
But the Red Wings got on the board 42 seconds later on Igor Larionov's power-play marker.

The Wings were on the power play again when Sergei Fedorov tied it 2:10 into the third period. He threaded a shot under Roy's right arm from the lower left circle after taking a pass from Lidstrom at the blue line.
Roy, who had allowed seven goals in his first seven home games in the postseason, kept this one tied with a spectacular stop on Vyacheslav Kozlov with 16:39 to go in regulation.
Roy dove from left to right and got his stick on the puck after Kozlov shot at a seemingly open net from the left circle.
